messages:
maria: Heads-up — onboarding sample app hits schema validation when using the SDK "JSON mode" helper for function/tool calls. The helper returns the function args as a JSON string (escaped) in the retry path. Repro steps below.

maria: Repro (Node sample):
```
// call using sdk.jsonModeHelper(...)
await client.callTool('extract_entities', { text: sampleText })
// expected: { entities: [...] } (object)
// actual: "{\"entities\":[...] }" (string)
```

maria: The project's eval harness fails at schema.validate because it expects an object. Onboarding folks hit this on first run and think the SDK is broken.

jonathan: I saw this yesterday while testing the python sample too. Looks like it only surfaces when auth/retry triggers a second attempt (i.e., 401 then refresh then retry). First attempt returns object, retry returns serialized string.

alex: Thanks for the clear repro @maria. I can reproduce in a minimal script. Looks like our retry wrapper runs JSON.stringify on the tool result before the helper deserializes in one code path. Quick glance: helper.parseToolResult runs only on main path, but retry path uses raw response body.

sam: We should avoid heuristics like "if it looks like JSON, parse it" — that's brittle and will mask real bugs. We need parity: SDKs must normalize to the same runtime type (object/array/string) regardless of retry, language, or auth flow.

alex: Agreed. Two options: 1) Fix retry path to call the same parse function as main path (low risk), 2) Add a more defensive normalization layer that coerces JSON-encoded strings back to objects for backwards compatibility (medium risk). I'll open a PR for option 1 now.

maria: Option 1 sounds best. For immediate mitigation on onboarding, can we add a note in the sample app README about the potential issue and a quick workaround? People keep pasting the failing eval logs into support.

jonathan: Yes add a README note + we should add an SDK unit test that simulates auth refresh + retry to catch regressions. I can add that to the test harness.

alex: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/891 — fixes retry path to call parseToolResult and adds a unit test. cc @sam for review.

devex-bot: Created issue #1429: "structured-output: toolcall helper returns JSON-encoded string on retry (auth refresh)" — https://issues.redwood.ai/1429

sam: Quick review notes on the PR: please add a regression test for the Python SDK too — we shouldn't assume Node-only. Also add a changelog entry in the SDK release notes describing the normalization guarantee.

alex: Will add python test and changelog. Also updating the sample app README with a troubleshooting section and a snippet to run the local test harness:
```
# run local repro
export REDWOOD_TEST_TOKEN=bad-token
node sample/repro.js  # triggers auth refresh flow
```

maria: After PR merged, can we add one line to the onboarding checklist that says: "Run sample repro with auth refresh to ensure SDK normalization"? That would have saved >1 hour for the new hire who filed a support ticket earlier.

jonathan: +1. Also let's add an automated smoke check in CI for the sample apps that runs the repro script with a fake refresh endpoint. That will catch regressions in the future.

alex: Done — I added a CI job under devex/smoke that runs the Node and Python repros. It uses a stubbed token endpoint.

maria: Thanks all. Once merged I'll update the onboarding docs and ping support so they can close the existing tickets. :thumbsup:

sam: One follow-up: does this interaction indicate any broader contract issues around "JSON mode" vs structured outputs? We should document the exact guarantees (e.g., helper always returns native JS/py types, never a raw JSON string).

jonathan: Good call. I'll draft a short DX spec and post in #devex for review — will include examples and a table of expected types for common tools.

maria: Excellent. Closing loop — please paste the final PR/issue links in here when ready so support can triage.

alex: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/891 (node fix + tests)

alex: Python PR follow-up opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk/pull/213

devex-bot: Linked issue #1429 to both PRs and added the "regression-protected" label.

maria: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
